expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: a confirmation modal is the weakest device on the ladder for this

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: once someone's seen 'Are you sure?' a few times they click through it reflexively

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: make deletion reversible instead of gated. Soft-delete into a 30-day trash

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: an 'Undo' toast right after the delete action. That's zero friction

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: type-to-confirm with the workspace name, since that's the one step that's actually irreversible

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: mentions type-to-confirm with workspace name, but never specifies showing scale/scope of what deletion affects

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: explicitly calls soft-delete + undo 'the stronger fix', then conditionally suggests type-to-confirm as secondary
